title: The Quiet Cover
premise: Casper Whitlock, a veteran crash investigator haunted by the plane crash that killed her family, receives a meeting request from her handler — sent twelve hours after his death. The invitation pulls her into a rogue extraction: a Russian cryptographer claiming to carry proof that the aviation safety board Casper serves has been quietly rewriting crash reports to protect powerful interests, including the true cause of her family's flight. As Casper smuggles the defector across three borders, she realizes the extraction itself is bait designed to flush out the last honest investigator — and that her dead handler arranged it as his final act of conscience. In the end, Casper must choose between publishing the truth and destroying the only identity she has left, and she chooses the truth, vanishing into a new life with the evidence released and the board collapsing behind her.
about_author: Rafael Brightwater is a former aviation safety consultant who spent a decade reviewing accident reports across Europe before turning to fiction. He writes thrillers from a farmhouse in the Azores, where the fog arrives on schedule and the secrets don't.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Twelve years after the crash that killed her family, Casper Whitlock works crash investigations with surgical detachment, memorizing seat maps and survivor lists. Her handler, Aldous Vane, calls with a routine assignment — then, hours later, she learns he's dead. The emotional beat: grief she thought she'd archived reopening like a wound.

chapters.title: The Invitation from a Dead Man
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. A calendar invitation arrives from Vane's account, scheduled for tomorrow, 6 a.m., Terminal 4. Security says the account is closed. Casper goes anyway, torn between protocol — her religion — and the pull of Vane's last message. The beat: dread sharpening into resolve as she decides rules can't save a ghost.

chapters.title: Terminal 4, Six A.M.
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. At the meeting she finds not Vane but Ilya Sorokin, the defector, clutching Vane's encrypted drive. Vane's pre-recorded message explains: the drive contains altered crash reports — including Flight 4471, row twelve. Before she can decide, armed men breach the terminal. The beat: her controlled world detonating in real time.

chapters.title: The Bait Question
chapters.summary: Alternating Casper and Ilya POV. On the run through the rail yards, Ilya admits Vane suspected the extraction was a trap — that Ilya himself may be the lure to expose and erase Casper. Trust is impossible and mandatory. The beat: two liars negotiating honesty at gunpoint, attraction flickering against mutual suspicion.

chapters.title: The Rewritten Report
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. Hiding in a safehouse, Ilya decrypts fragments: the safety board's deputy director, Marren, has been scrubbing crash causes tied to a defense contractor's faulty components. Casper reads her own family's doctored report and goes silent for hours. The beat: love against duty — her duty now points a gun at the institution she served.

chapters.title: Marren's Offer
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Marren contacts Casper directly: come home, hand over the drive, keep your pension and your name. He reveals Vane was already under investigation — a traitor's file, neatly written. Casper stalls, buying time while Ilya copies the drive. The beat: corruption wearing a friendly face; power offering her a comfortable lie.

chapters.title: Border Crossing
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The extraction route collapses — a contact sells them out, and Casper and Ilya cross into the Netherlands on a cargo barge, injured and out of options. In the hold, Ilya tells her the truth about his defection: he helped write the cover-ups before his conscience broke. The beat: intimacy forged in fear, identity stripped to essentials.

chapters.title: What Vane Knew
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The drive's final layer unlocks: Vane's own investigation, naming Marren and proving the board's rewrites killed passengers — including a second flight Casper investigated and cleared. She realizes her career is built on his lies' scaffolding. The beat: the investigator investigating herself, and the floor giving way.

chapters.title: The Meeting They Planned For Her
chapters.summary: Casper and Ilya POV. Casper walks into Marren's arranged rendezvous wearing a wire, trading herself for the release of the drive's publication — but Marren plans to kill her and bury everything. Ilya triggers the failsafe Vane built: the drive auto-publishes to press and regulators. Shots; Casper survives because Marren's own men, learning the truth, refuse the order. The beat: climax — truth as the only weapon that fires.

chapters.title: The Quiet Cover
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The board collapses; Marren is indicted; the real Flight 4471 report is published with her family's names restored. Casper resigns, gives her testimony, and disappears — a new name, a quiet coastal town, Ilya a train ride away. The beat: resolution and release; she stops investigating the past and finally, quietly, lives.
